subject: Commit verification + billing discrepancy — Clearline renewal (action items)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Commit verification + billing discrepancy — Clearline renewal (action items)

Team —

Flagging Clearline Systems (renewal due 2027-09-15). Finance spotted a billing variance in Q2 invoice vs. the committed ARR in SFDC: looks like an underbilled seat tier and one unrecognized add-on. We need a quick reconciliation so renewal forecast reflects the true committed ARR and we can surface churn risk.

Asks:
- Marissa: confirm the contract line items and whether the add-on was an approved change (attach SOW if available).
- Naomi: update the renewal probability in the book and note the cause (billing mismatch).
- David: run a short ledger check against AP and confirm whether Clearline paid the Q2 invoice in full or disputed it.

I attached a preliminary MRR worksheet — please annotate rows that change the committed ARR. Let's aim to close this loop EOD tomorrow (21 Jun) so finance has an answer for the pause request from AP.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Clearline_MRR_breakdown_Q2.xlsx (xlsx), SOW_Clearline_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit verification + billing discrepancy — Clearline renewal (action items)

Rishi —

Quick update: I pulled the CS notes and the signed amendment (attached). The add-on was a one-time premium pipeline connector that was agreed in May but the amendment was routed via e-sign incorrectly and landed on "pending signature" in our DocuSign logs until June 3. The amendment references a billing cadence change that should have increased monthly billing by $12k starting May. SFDC did not reflect the amendment until Jun 8, which explains the Q2 underbilling.

Impact on committed ARR: the amendment, once applied, pushes committed ARR +$144k annualized. I flagged the account as "billing reconciliation required" in the CRM and set next steps:
- Confirm invoice applied retroactively or issue a corrective invoice (David)
- Move renewal probability from 75% to 65% until payment / corrective invoice resolved (Naomi)
- Coordinate a one-week credit hold if AP does not confirm payment (Rishi)

I've attached the signed amendment PDF (SOW_Clearline_v2.pdf).

—Marissa
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW_Clearline_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Jared Collins <jared.collins@clearline.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts-payable@clearline.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit verification + billing discrepancy — Clearline renewal (action items)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the transparency. AP confirms they received an invoice for May that was short the connector line item; that was an internal routing error on our side. We can either accept a corrective invoice for May (net +$12k) or apply the delta to the July invoice — whichever is less operationally painful.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood issue a corrected invoice that references the amendment so our AP audit logs match?
2) Please confirm there will be no immediate change to the production service if we push the delta to July — we need assurance no suspension will be triggered.

I copied AP for confirmation of the payment window.

—Jared
Director, Platform Ops
Clearline Systems

External attachment references: our AP policy doc (not included)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit verification + billing discrepancy — Clearline renewal (action items)

Team —

I checked the ledger and AP status: AP at Clearline shows the May invoice paid on June 7 but with a manual note "amount short - connector item omitted." Their payment reconciled to the net amount, not the amended amount. We can issue a corrective invoice that will appear as a credit memo + new invoice (preferred for audit trail).

Implications: corrective invoice is straightforward but will re-open the dispute timeline (AP may take 30 days to remit). If we push the delta to July, we can avoid a corrective invoice but lose a clean audit trail on the May month.

Recommendation: issue a corrected invoice that references the signed amendment and include a 14-day courtesy window before any collection/hold actions. This balances audit integrity and customer goodwill.

I'll prepare the invoice language and copy the accounting team.

—David
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 16:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit verification + billing discrepancy — Clearline renewal (action items)

Thanks all — good thread. Final actions I captured: 
1) David: send corrected invoice referencing SOW_Clearline_v2 and include 14-day courtesy window (send by EOD Wed 23 Jun).
2) Marissa: update SFDC committed ARR to include the amendment +$144k and add a "billing_recon" note with the DocuSign timestamp.
3) Naomi: set renewal probability to 65% and add a churn-risk flag with rationale (underbilled / payment timeline).
4) I will reach out to Jared to confirm that issuing a corrected invoice is acceptable and that no immediate service restrictions will be applied while this is resolved.

Please reply with status updates inline. If we can't confirm corrected invoice issuance by Wed EOD, we'll queue a one-week credit hold as contingency and escalate to CS leadership.

—Rishi
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
